name: Collar stays

lead: Collar stays are thin rigid strips slipped into pockets under the points of a dress shirt collar to keep them flat and sharp.
They are used for a crisp neckline. No scholarly evidence exists; it is a tailoring convention.

paras: The stiff strip prevents the collar tip from curling or bending.
Plastic stays can warp or break and should be removed before laundry or ironing; metal stays last longer. Benefits are small and temporary.
